description: NFC boundary — PASS: jcs-n preserves decomposed code points as-is. Key U+0041 U+030A (A + combining ring above) is two UTF-16 code units; jcs-n sorts it after 'B' (one code unit) and serialises the raw bytes, producing a different digest than an NFC-normalising construction. Motivated by Joel Hillier's on-list finding (2026-07-27): no published corpus exercises this boundary.
note: The key U+0041 U+030A (A + U+030A combining ring above, decomposed 'Å') is 2 UTF-16 code units; RFC 8785 §3.2.3 sorts by (UTF-16-length, UTF-16-code-units), so 'B' (len 1) sorts before this key (len 2). jcs-n leaves the code points unchanged; the UTF-8 encoding of U+030A is 0xCC 0x8A, giving pre_image_bytes_hex ending ...41cc8a.... See jcs-n-nfc-contrast-01 for the contrast digest a normalising profile would produce.
